candidates.Core content: Algorithms; data structures; discrete models; computability; complexity; randomized/approximation ideas; cryptographic intuition.
candidates.Exit capability: Reconstruct algorithmic tradeoffs, reason about tractability, and detect when 'AI solved it' hides computational or verification costs.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Scientific computing is numerical; it does not substitute for general computer science.
candidates.Decision: ADMIT unless existing modules can absorb it without distortion.

candidates.Core content: Software architecture; testing; versioning; OS/processes; databases; networks; distributed consensus/failure; observability; privacy; secure development.
candidates.Exit capability: Design and audit a networked software service with explicit failure, security, data, and operational boundaries.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Advanced civilization and AI infrastructure are software/networked systems; this is currently implicit.
candidates.Decision: ADMIT unless TS23 is broadened enough without becoming unteachable.

candidates.Core content: Climate/energy balance; atmosphere/ocean circulation; water; soils; biogeochemical cycles; ecosystems; population/ecology; resource flows; environmental risk.
candidates.Exit capability: Trace coupled physical-biological-human constraints and identify hard planetary/transport/resource limits on interventions.
candidates.Why current core may not cover it: Physics + biology do not automatically produce usable Earth-system intuition.
candidates.Decision: KEEP AS CANDIDATE; backtest against climate, agriculture, water, biodiversity, mining, disaster cases.
